title: The Courier Who Ran Off With the Mail
story: Across the glass desert sprints Glisterdune, a long-legged mirage-thing with the village mail satchel bouncing on its back — a whole winter's worth of letters and a pouch of silver acorns. By the time Mr 6 unfurls the sail of a borrowed wind-skiff, the courier is already 9 leagues ahead and shimmering. Mr 6 does not panic; he does arithmetic.
question: Glisterdune runs at a steady 12 leagues per hour with a 9-league head start, and Mr 6's wind-skiff sails at 15 leagues per hour. How many leagues will Mr 6 have sailed by the moment he draws level with the courier?
solution: Closing speed: 15 − 12 = 3 leagues gained every hour.
Time to erase the 9-league gap: 9 ÷ 3 = 3 hours.
praise: Comparing the two speeds was exactly the right instinct — after finding the hours, one more step turns that time into leagues sailed.
hint: Each hour, how much of the 9-league gap disappears? Find the hours first, then ask how far the skiff travelled in that time.
victory: Glisterdune skids to a stop in a spray of glass sand, laughing, and hands over the satchel — any hero who can out-think a mirage deserves the mail, and a new volunteer postal runner.
imagePrompt: A shimmering long-legged mirage creature with a bulging mail satchel racing across a dawn-lit glass desert, chased by a small caped numeral 6 knight steering a little sail-skiff that kicks up glittering dust, bright and thrilling.
